items.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 18 at 1:41PM EST until November 22 at 7:00AM EST by NWS Jacksonville FL
items.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 6 to
10 feet. For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Southeast Georgia and Northeast Florida Beaches.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 7 AM EST Sunday. For
the High Rip Current Risk, through Sunday morning.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
items.instruction:
Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

items.headline: Flood Watch issued November 18 at 12:30AM EST until November 20 at 7:00PM EST by NWS Jacksonville FL
items.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...A portion of northeast Florida, including the following
areas, Coastal Duval, Coastal Flagler, Eastern Clay, Eastern
Putnam, Inland Flagler, Northeast Coastal St. Johns, Northern
Inland St. Johns, South Central Duval, Southeast Coastal St. Johns,
Southern Inland St. Johns, Trout River, Western Clay, Western
Duval, Western Putnam and Western St. Johns.

* WHEN...Through Friday evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Several rounds of heavy rainfall are expected to repeatedly occur
in the watch area through the end of the week. Repeated rounds of
heavy rainfall will result in the potential for urban and small
stream flooding for the coastal areas of northeast Florida. Total
rainfall forecast through Friday night is around 3 to 8 inches
with locally higher amounts up to 12 inches or more.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
items.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

items.headline: Small Craft Advisory issued November 18 at 1:36PM EST until November 22 at 7:00AM EST by NWS Jacksonville FL
items.description:
* WHAT...Northeast winds 20 to 30 kt with gusts up to 35 kt and
seas 9 to 14 ft.

* WHERE...All Southeast Georgia and Northeast Florida coastal
waters from Altamaha Sound GA to Flagler Beach FL out to 60 NM.

* WHEN...Until 7 AM EST Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Conditions will be hazardous to small craft.
items.instruction:
Inexperienced mariners, especially those operating smaller
vessels, should avoid navigating in hazardous conditions.
